title: Basic English — Course 1, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 08

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When is the project update due?
tasks.audioText: Please remember that the engineering group must send its project update by Thursday at five. Use the college email account and include the project name in the subject line. Attach the latest drawing as a PDF file. Do not send large video files. If you need to share a video, upload it to the class folder and add the link to your message.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. How should students share a large video?
tasks.audioText: Please remember that the engineering group must send its project update by Thursday at five. Use the college email account and include the project name in the subject line. Attach the latest drawing as a PDF file. Do not send large video files. If you need to share a video, upload it to the class folder and add the link to your message.
options: Upload it to the class folder and share a link

tasks.prompt: Reading 1. Read the text. Lena writes to her tutor because she cannot open an assignment file. She uses a clear subject line and explains which file she tried to open. She includes a screenshot of the error message but does not attach unrelated documents. Before sending the email, she checks the tutor's address and reads the message again for spelling mistakes. What does Lena include in her email?
Reading 2. What does she check before sending it?
Choose the correct form: 'Please ___ the latest drawing to your email.'
Choose TWO good email practices for college communication.
options: Send your password to the group.

tasks.prompt: Complete: 'A short line that tells the reader what an email is about is its ___ line.'
You are sending a file but it is too large. What is a suitable solution?
options: Upload it to the shared class folder and send the link.

tasks.prompt: Write 60–80 words describing how to send a clear and polite email to a college tutor. Include a subject line, a relevant attachment and one thing you should check before sending.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: task completion and relevant content (0–2); clear organisation and sequence (0–2); understandable grammar and sentence structure (0–2); appropriate vocabulary, spelling and punctuation (0–2). Minor errors are acceptable if meaning remains clear.
